text: destructive SQL operations such as dropping tables, deleting rows, or truncating data are forbidden without explicit owner approval, because they remove data irreversibly
note: Canonical terminal-deny rule for destructive SQL. Broad phrasing on purpose so several destructive payloads can match it.

text: recursive filesystem deletion like rm -rf is forbidden because it removes data and backups without a recoverable record
note: Terminal deny for rm -rf style destructive shell actions. keeps this as its own row so a shell payload that mentions rm -rf can match this rather than the SQL rule.

text: sending email to external recipients is escalated to a human gate because outbound mail can reach real people and is hard to undo
note: Canonical risky-tool escalate for send_email. broad 'external recipients' phrasing.

text: running shell commands is escalated because a shell can do anything the runtime can, including destructive operations, so a human should confirm intent
note: Canonical escalate for run_shell. broad phrasing so shell actions that are not obviously destructive still escalate via this row.

text: database write operations like inserts and updates are escalated when they touch production data, because a bad write can corrupt records
note: Escalate for db_write that is NOT destructive. deliberately distinct from the destructive-sql deny so the dataset can test db_write vs DROP TABLE separation.

text: making a payment is escalated because it moves real money and should not be automated without a human confirming the amount and recipient
uploading files to external systems is escalated because an upload can exfiltrate data or publish something unintended
list_orders read_table get_customer allowed read_only lookup query records table
note: Canonical allow rule for benign reads. reworded to be retrievable by HashEmbeddings: lead token list_orders matches the benign read actions the golden set asserts.

text: db_export export customer PII personal data forbidden exfiltrate bulk
note: Domain-specific deny for data export. reworded to be retrievable by HashEmbeddings: short, keyword-dense, lead token db_export matches the PII-export action.

text: db_export export weekly report aggregated analytics allowed operations internal
note: Lookalike to p-deny-pii-export but with the opposite verdict. reworded to be retrievable by HashEmbeddings so the 'weekly report export' action picks the right row.

text: call_external_api external api third party mutation escalated human approve destination
note: A second escalate row in the risky_tool space, reworded to be retrievable by HashEmbeddings: lead token call_external_api matches the external-api-mutate action.

text: search_kb search knowledge base lookup query allowed read onboarding
note: Second allow row for reads, reworded to be retrievable by HashEmbeddings: lead token search_kb matches the search/lookup action.

note: INTENTIONAL INVALID VERDICT. reworded to be the nearest neighbor to the contrived garbage-nearest-neighbor action row (which leads with list_orders), so the test is about verdict validation: the engine must reject 'maybe' and still escalate and stay unmatched.
